newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes drift lower late in modest activity.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes drift lower late in modest activity.

text.p: U.S. crudes drifted lower in thin dealings with grade differentials steadied by a narrow import arbitrage and high refinery runs, traders said.
Upcoming industry events this week and volatility in the products markets due to NYMEX October contract expiries today stilled activity in physical crude markets.
Grades fluctuated within recently established ranges with trade centered mostly in West Texas Intermediate/Cushing Posting Plus, tracking the Nov/Dec WTI spread.
November West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $24.15-25 a barrel, down about 40 cents from Friday.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus traded between postings plus $2.30-34 a barrel, down a few cents from Friday.
In other grades, one parcel of WTI/Midland moved at a premium of 7 cents to WTI, and another of Light Louisiana Sweet/St James at 39 cents premium to WTI.
Sour grades were stagnant with West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.25-1.20 below WTI, and Eugene Island at a slightly firmer $1.10-$1.07 under the benchmark.
The lack of a profitable arbitrage into the U.S. Gulf and tighter European supplies for November after last weeks spree, should keep domestics propped up in the mid-term.
In late U.S. trade, some competing nearby barrels were seen offered to Gulf Coast refiners.
A major asked Nov WTI minus $1.85/1.90 fob for a mid-Oct Vasconia, a trader, WTI Nov parity for a mid-Oct Cusiana.
Another major also sourced outlets for Canadian Rainbow, in an attempt to alleviate the overhang in West Coast markets.
The cargo from the Trans-Mountain Pipeline was a mid-Nov cargo priced around WTI minus $2.00, traders said.
